paragraphs: What is worth exploring is tree care, accurate records and teamwork. Liking plants is only a starting point; you also need to be willing to check the work object, accept training, keep watching for environmental change and be clear about the tasks you cannot yet take on.

Tree pruning may involve heights, falling branches, vehicles, power machinery and power lines. Personal skill certificates, the organisation's work arrangements and statutory approval are each verified separately; neither the occupational title nor a paper exercise score automatically grants work authority.

This occupation corresponds to O*NET37-3013.00, pruning trees or shrubs to serve clearance, appearance, health and value. Turf maintenance, plant protection application, forestry technology and equipment operation each have different task scopes.

Start with the fictional four-tree record in the entry module: organise the first version, then handle the F1 tree number correction and the F2 added cable information. Use pen and paper or an offline spreadsheet only: do not enter a site, prune, climb or use machinery or chemicals.
What kind of person suits a tree trimmer?

Observe whether you can match tree numbers accurately, distinguish a record from a diagnosis, check the items awaiting confirmation and pass changes to the responsible people. Safety boundaries, physical adaptation and team communication need to be considered together.

The exercise on this page is an editorial career exploration and cannot prove ability in tree climbing, chainsaw work, lifting equipment or work near power lines, nor replace employer training, professional assessment or the applicable licensing.

Positive signals are patiently checking records, being willing to correct errors and keep versions, reporting uncertain tree condition, ownership or cable information first, and accepting review and division of work in the real job.

Signals for caution are declaring a tree safe from a photograph, treating a draft as approval, or skipping checks for speed. When applying, also ask clearly about work height, equipment, weather arrangements, training and actual pay.

Compare the three versions of the tree numbers and pending items, explaining which record each round of feedback affects, who confirms it and which statuses remain unresolved; then judge whether you are willing to keep doing care, records and coordination long term.

This occupation's identity is tree trimmer O*NET37-3013.00, focused on tree pruning and care. General landscaping maintenance, chemical application, equipment operation and technical assessment staff on the same landscaping project do not thereby swap duties.

Inputs include the tree number, location, care purpose, tree condition records, surrounding road and utility information, management requirements and task arrangements. First check which tree a record corresponds to, keep unknown items pending, and do not write an observation directly as a disease diagnosis.

The editorial suggestion is to check the object and purpose first, then list the questions that need confirmation by the manager, a professional or the utility. Whether work can proceed is assessed by the actual responsible people; complete paper records do not mean the site is safe or the work is approved.

Outputs include the pruning and care completed as confirmed, the clearing of debris and traceable records. Real execution also needs professional skills, equipment and site control; this page describes occupational tasks only and gives no beginner operating steps.

Ground-level care and work at height or near utilities have different conditions. Height, weather, tree condition, pedestrians and traffic, equipment and cable changes may all affect the arrangement and should be reassessed by the corresponding responsible person, without copying the previous site's conclusion.

Communicate with the crew lead, ground support staff, the landscaping manager and, where needed, utility professionals. Say so promptly when conditions do not match; receiving a task must not be understood as holding all equipment and specialised work authority.

The typical United States EMP entry education for this occupation is high school or equivalent, with short-term on-the-job training as the typical preparation; this is not a uniform Chinese education threshold, nor does it mean work at height or near power lines can be taken on independently by an untrained person after a short time.

A delivery keeps the tree number, location, date, before and after status, task and review records and makes the unresolved items and their responsible person clear. A public portfolio uses fictional data only; real locations and organisational material require checking authorisation, and a record cannot pass itself off as work approval.

The two task lines can be divided into routine tree care and complex on-site pruning, sharing object checking and coordination. The following is an editorial task summary, and real work must be arranged by the organisation according to tree condition, environment, staff ability and the applicable rules.
Routine tree care line

Check the tree number and goal → bring together the observation material → give the task to the responsible person to check → carry it out as confirmed → clear debris and record → review the follow-up care
Care results, task records and items to be tracked
Work-at-height or near-utility task line

Check the object and surrounding conditions → professional assessment → check the specialist staff, equipment and authority → carry it out per the site arrangement → review the result → keep the unresolved status
The results of confirmed tasks and the professional review records
Shared professional foundation
Tree knowledge · accurate records · environmental checking · tool and equipment ability · teamwork · boundaries of authority
How are routine care and complex on-site pruning distinguished?

Both are tree pruning tasks, but the working conditions change the staff ability, equipment and management requirements. Routine care focuses on continued maintenance, while work at height or near utilities adds specialised risk and a chain of responsibility; the table below is an editorial comparison, not a work plan.
Core purpose
Maintain appearance, health and clearance according to the confirmed tree care goal, accurately recording what has been done and what still needs tracking.
Handles the pruning needs arising from a particular tree, location and surrounding conditions under professional assessment and site control.
Main object and basis
The tree number, care goal, observation records, manager requirements and crew task; unknown tree condition must go to a professional to check.
Tree condition, work height, utility and traffic conditions, professional assessment, equipment and staff and the applicable management requirements.
Core process
Check the records and task, carry it out as the crew confirmed, clear debris, keep records and track the care.
Check the site conditions and the specialised boundary, carry it out after confirmation by the corresponding responsible person and reassess if a condition changes.
Main outputs
Tree care results, accurate tree number records and follow-up care issues.
Records of the specific task completed, professional review opinions and unresolved items.
Accountable party
Pruning staff complete tasks within their training and authority, the manager specifies the care goal and the crew lead organises and checks the actual arrangement.

The organisation arranges the professional assessment and the staffing and equipment; matters such as proximity to power lines require the corresponding professionals, and the person keeping records cannot grant themselves specialised authority.
Mode of coordination
Communicate tree numbers, tasks and changes under the confirmed division of work and keep the ground team's information consistent.
Work with the site lead, ground support and, where needed, utility professionals, and report changes promptly.
Delivery boundary
A care record cannot replace a tree disease diagnosis, a tree safety assessment or felling approval.

Work-at-height skills and near-power-line ability, equipment operating authority and the organisation's site arrangement are each checked separately and are not interchangeable under one occupational title.
Key occupational judgements

Check the object, purpose and unknown conditions first, then give the questions to the actual responsible people. The following is an editorial record self-check and gives no guidance on cut positions, climbing, equipment or power line operation.
Are the tree number, location and care purpose in the record consistent?
Which items are recorded information and which still need professional checking?
Is the old arrangement still being followed after a change in height, cables or weather?
Which tree number or pending item did the feedback change, and is the revision traceable?

Change only the records affected by the feedback and keep the old version. In the exercise F1 requires moving the T02 tree condition note to T03; this is not copying it to both trees and not rewriting the tree condition yourself as diagnosed.
Are personal ability, organisational arrangements and statutory approval written as if they were the same?

Verify skill training, equipment use and the actual project rules separately. The work-at-height item in the 2026 special operations catalogue has a specific scope of application, and a height of two metres alone cannot be used to declare that every tree pruning post requires the same certificate.
Which tree numbers, versions and pending statuses must be kept after delivery?
Object checking | tree and care goal | confirm the tree number, location and pruning purpose and tell the responsible person where the material is inconsistent.
Tree care | professional task execution | carry out pruning and care within actual ability and task scope and pass suspected pest or structural problems to a professional to check.

Tools and equipment | preparation and maintenance | this occupation involves cutting tools, power tools, chipping equipment and vehicle-mounted lifting equipment; actual operation requires the corresponding training and arrangements, and this page gives no practical tutorial.
On-site coordination | people and environment | work with the ground team, watch for falling branches, roads, pedestrians, weather and utility changes, and report along the chain of responsibility.
Debris clearing and review | results and records | clear the branches and leaves from pruning, check what was actually completed and keep the tree numbers and unresolved items.

Technical communication | care and management | explain the care material and follow-up issues to the manager; whether estimating, supervision or professional advice belongs to this post must be checked separately.
Section heading | the work environment and working style of tree trimmers

This occupation is mainly outdoor tree work in a crew, with some tasks in the upper canopy or using vehicle-mounted lifting equipment. The site conditions vary with tree condition, weather, roads and utilities, and suitability for the work cannot be judged from an interest in plants alone.

Organisations and locations | parks, roads, housing or other green spaces may have tree care needs; tree ownership and management responsibility must be checked. The Chinese historical recruitments are mixed landscaping and care posts and cannot be used to presume dedicated pruning tasks at height.

Materials and tools | tree records, location material, care requirements and site arrangements are the work inputs. Hand cutting tools, power cutting tools and lifting or chipping equipment appear in the occupational material, but the equipment ability and licensing must be checked in reality and explorers are not required to buy tools.

Work is carried out under the division of duties confirmed by the responsible person and professionals. United States OSHA material emphasises on-site hazard assessment and protection; it serves as a reference for United States safety responsibility only and is not treated as directly applicable Chinese law.

Scheduling and intensity | the BLS combined grounds maintenance group notes outdoor work in varied weather, repetitive physical labour and some seasonality. This is the occupation group's background; the specific Chinese working hours, emergency tasks and weather stoppage arrangements for this occupation are verified per post.
When communicating, report the tree number, location, date, the changes found and the pending items, and do not let vague description or personal guesswork replace a clear record.

Review and responsibility | tree condition and the working environment are checked by the corresponding professionals and the organisation is responsible for the actual task arrangement. Urban tree felling and utility-line pruning rules each have their own boundaries, and the person organising records cannot approve or carry them out.

Quality requirements | the correct task object, a clear care goal, traceable records, feedback on changes and truthful statuses for unknown items. A paper portfolio tests records and communication only, and practical competence still needs training and professional supervision.
Professional basis and boundaries of application
The O*NET37-3013.00 definition, tasks and RC interests; a United States occupational record does not directly establish a Chinese qualification.
The BLS combined grounds maintenance group's work background, with the EMP37-3013 entry route and employment projection for this occupation marked separately.
The Mile 2025 historical announcements: two employers' combined landscaping and care conditions, not a national starting salary for this occupation or confirmed vacancies.
China's 2026 urban greening regulations and special operations catalogue: urban tree management and the specific operations items are checked separately.
OSHA tree work guidance and ISA knowledge certification: a United States responsibility reference and a voluntary professional certificate, which cannot replace Chinese licensing or on-site ability.

Tree trimmers prune trees or shrubs to serve clearance, appearance, health and value; the tasks may involve heights, equipment and utilities. Actual execution depends on professional skills, site assessment and the crew's division of work, and general landscaping maintenance, chemical application and forestry technology duties cannot all be merged into it.
Under the guidance of forestry or conservation professionals, compiles forest resource data, provides technical support or leads related work, producing survey records and technical reports.
Maintains green spaces and plants comprehensively, including turf, planting, watering and some pruning; the coverage differs from a dedicated tree trimming post.
Handles, mixes or applies plant protection chemicals and records treatment tasks; the application conditions and licensing are checked by jurisdiction and actual work.
Operates agricultural equipment for sowing, harvesting and similar production tasks, with the focus on equipment and agricultural production processes.

paragraphs: Routine tree care direction
Carries out pruning, debris clearing and follow-up records according to the confirmed tree care goal. The specific techniques and tasks are confirmed by professionals and the responsible person.
A task direction within this occupation, focused on continued tree care; turf maintenance or all chemical application work is not merged into it.
Willing to learn about trees patiently, check the object and purpose, and accept training and repeated care records.
Work-at-height or near-utility pruning direction
Completes pruning at a specific location under professional assessment, with the corresponding staff and equipment and the site arrangement, and keeps the review status.
May still fall within this occupation but adds work-at-height, power line and on-site coordination requirements; general pruning experience does not automatically prove specialised ability.
Willing to check ability and authority carefully and learn through proper training and supervision; explore the task requirements first and do not attempt high-risk operations on your own.
Forestry and conservation technicians
The focus shifts to resource data, technical support and forest management; tree pruning experience cannot replace survey, data or technical report ability.
Prefers resource survey and technical records and is willing to add study and on-site ability for the target post.
Landscaping and grounds maintenance workers
Faces broader green space maintenance involving turf, plants and grounds; the hours, equipment and requirements of combined maintenance and dedicated tree pruning are checked separately.
Wants to take part in comprehensive plant care and is willing to compare real post tasks rather than focusing only on tree pruning at height.
Pesticide handlers, sprayers and applicators, vegetation
Chemicals, the target, the environment and application records become key; tree pruning ability cannot replace chemical knowledge, licensing or professional treatment judgement.
More interested in pests and diseases and treatment records, and willing to check the local application requirements and real training conditions.
Agricultural equipment operators
Focused on agricultural machinery operation and production tasks; sharing the use of equipment does not make it interchangeable with tree climbing, lifting or chipping ability.
More willing to learn around agricultural equipment and production processes and to check the actual machinery category and operating conditions.
How should you choose between tree care directions and adjacent occupations?

First distinguish routine care and complex on-site tasks within this occupation, then compare forestry technology, combined landscaping care, plant protection and agricultural equipment operation. The tasks in the table are an editorial summary of official definitions and the suitability signals are exploration suggestions; the actual Chinese post title, equipment and qualifications are checked against recruitment and the jurisdiction.

Complete the paper record on this page first and judge whether you like object checking, change feedback and coordination. If interest shifts to resource survey, combined care, chemicals or agricultural machinery, add ability for the target occupation's output and do not presume a direct transfer from one tree pruning experience.

This occupation's tasks are based on O*NET37-3013.00, and the four adjacent occupations use 19-4071.00, 37-3011.00, 37-3012.00 and 45-2091.00 respectively. The definitions describe the United States occupational scope and set no uniform Chinese entry requirement; the authority for work at height, equipment, chemical application and technical assessment is checked separately.

Once the task direction is clear, look at which records AI can assist with and which on-site judgements and responsibilities still rest with people; text generation ability is not used to infer that the whole occupation can be replaced.

At the capability level, text tools can be used to organise tree number records or a handover draft, which is an editorial suggestion. First compare the fictional material item by item against the original and check whether the tree numbers, locations, statuses and responsible people are accurate; generating more text does not equal a tree condition diagnosis, an on-site safety assessment or practical ability.

Record organisation, professional judgement and on-site execution are kept separate. Tree condition, weather, falling branches, roads and power lines cannot be confirmed by a generated paragraph; a paper draft does not automatically become a work plan or an approved task.

Insufficient evidence: this round obtained no occupational-level AI adoption rate or net time saving research for tree trimmers. Product features, cross-industry frameworks and public discussion cannot prove that this occupation has adopted AI widely, and adoption still requires stating the real tasks, inputs, human review and actual results.

First establish the task, data source and authority, use only approved material and check the output. Tree numbers, locations and crew information cannot be presumed uploadable just because they can be copied; the fictional exercise needs no AI service and can still complete every item.
The O*NET record for this occupation includes pruning and care, tools and equipment, debris clearing and teamwork, but the task list does not prove that a tool is effective or has been adopted.

Generating a task list is not approval. The actual tree condition assessment, staff ability, the organisation's task arrangement and the applicable project requirements must be confirmed by the corresponding responsible people; AI output cannot grant work authority. Nor can the EMP total employment projection prove an AI-caused change in posts.

Responsibility still needs to be clear: the record keeper checks the object and version, professionals assess and the organisation arranges the actual task. AI output cannot grant personal skill, equipment or on-site authority, nor replace management approval or a signed review.

Insufficient evidence: this round has no net employment change research for tree trimmers attributable to AI alone. The EMP occupational total projection is not an AI substitution rate and cannot directly represent the Chinese market or an individual's probability of unemployment.

NIST provides a voluntary cross-industry risk management method supporting consideration of purpose, reliability and responsibility; the tree record application on this page is an editorial inference, not an effectiveness experiment for this occupation.

Can a text tool judge tree condition for me?

A text draft cannot be used to declare a tree healthy, safe or ready to work on. The editorial suggestion is to use fictional records for organisation and review only and to pass real problems to the corresponding professionals; this page provides no evidence of model diagnostic effect or reliability.
Does an image recognition result equal an on-site assessment?

It cannot be presumed. An image or text does not cover the full tree condition, environment and work conditions, and this page has no verifiable diagnostic trial for this occupation; the actual professional assessment and the organisation's arrangement cannot be replaced by model output.
Does access to records mean they can be uploaded to a tool?

First check the material owner, purpose, recipient and retention arrangement, and do not presume it can be uploaded just because it can be accessed. Career exploration uses fictional records only, and whether real organisational material may be processed should be confirmed with the responsible person.

No evidence of an AI independent net employment change was obtained. The EMP total growth of 4.2% includes many factors and cannot be broken into an AI gain or loss figure, nor does it represent Chinese posts or an individual's probability of being hired.
Can United States material directly determine Chinese on-site authority?

It does not apply automatically. The United States tasks and safety method can provide verification questions, and the Chinese qualifications and project rules should be checked against the current jurisdiction and the actual organisational arrangement; a generated summary cannot change the scope of application.

Check the task, material permissions, tree number and location, status and output responsibility. Insufficient evidence: this round did not obtain a national median wage or percentile distribution for the exact occupation of tree trimmers in mainland China. Public wage entries from the National Bureau of Statistics and related recruitment notices were checked; general landscaping maintenance notices can only serve as a proxy for historical positions and cannot be used to fill in national statistics for this occupation.

When comparing pay, first verify job tasks, monthly wage composition, working hours, rest, overtime, social insurance, and equipment training. Dedicated high-work tree pruning and mixed landscaping maintenance cannot be compared directly based only on a similar name or a single quote.

Total receipts from self-employed services must also separate business costs such as equipment, transport, and personnel from personal income. Employee quotes, self-employed receipts, and take-home amounts each have their own basis, and this page does not assume uniform costs or a fixed number of working days per year.

The historical notice from Mile City dated 2025-04-22 contains two different employers: Chengfa Landscaping general landscaping maintenance and Yunnan Jirui landscaping maintenance. Both share one notice and each has its own quote; this does not claim they are dedicated tree pruning or currently open positions.

That historical notice lists no clear closing date, and this round did not confirm that it is still recruiting today. Full daily working hours, monthly wage composition, and dedicated high-work tasks are not disclosed, and the page status of “valid” cannot be understood as the position being currently open.
Tree pruning pay in China: historical maintenance samples and the national gap

Chengfa Landscaping: 2300—3800 yuan per month; 10 people for mixed landscaping maintenance, 4 rest days a month, and work safety liability insurance purchased. The notice does not specify pre-tax take-home pay or monthly wage composition, and this is not interpreted as the five social insurances.

Yunnan Jirui: 2850—3500 yuan per month; 6 people for historical 2025 landscaping maintenance, listing commuter transport, holiday benefits, work injury insurance, and accident insurance, with no full working hours or dedicated high-work tasks listed. Current open status is unconfirmed, and the five social insurances of other positions in the same notice are not applied.

Chengfa Landscaping historical 2025 landscaping maintenance: ages 20—55, with relevant work experience; the age limit may be relaxed appropriately for those with related landscaping experience, and veterans are preferred; mixed tasks include construction, nursery stock and flower maintenance, pest and disease control, nursery stock and lawn pruning, and river salvage. The notice lists no education requirement for this position, and the junior high school requirement of an adjacent watchkeeping position is not applied.

Yunnan Jirui's landscaping maintenance position lists only hard work and obedience to management, and does not describe dedicated tree pruning assignments; this cannot be used to lower safety training or qualification requirements.
The two employers are not two independent documents, and they are not a complete regional market sample; two quotes cannot be used to infer demand rates or starting pay for dedicated tree pruning.
A small number of historical mixed positions cannot form a national wage distribution for this occupation; when job tasks, pay method, working hours, and costs are unknown, keep the gap.

Actual paid arrangements affect personal income comparisons. Ask clearly how seasons, weather, or task interruptions are handled, judge by the contract and the real schedule, and do not use calendar days to estimate guaranteed income.

Insufficient evidence: this round has no occupation-level data on a causal effect of AI adoption on wages for tree trimmers in China. Feature changes in recording tools cannot be converted into a pay cut percentage, and real tasks, adoption methods, and pay conditions still need verification.

Chinese quotes retain the employer, location, job scope, notice date, and unit; US hourly wages, broad industry averages, or high project prices are not used to fill in national statistics for this occupation. The current open status of historical notices is unconfirmed.

US 2025 wage data are the employee distribution for this occupation, 37-3013: annual median 50,960 US dollars and hourly median 24.50 US dollars. Both the annual and hourly figures are official listed values; the statistics are not an individual's actual annual take-home pay, self-employed receipts, or Chinese quotes.

The 10th percentile annual wage in 2025 is 37,940 US dollars, corresponding to the official hourly listing of 18.24 US dollars. A percentile is a position in the employee wage distribution, not an entry level or a starting pay guarantee.

The 90th percentile annual wage in 2025 is 80,310 US dollars, corresponding to the official hourly listing of 38.61 US dollars. A high percentile cannot be labeled a senior level, and it does not guarantee an individual's annual hours and income.

EMP for this occupation shows 4.2% employment growth from 2025 to 2035, from 70,600 to 73,600 people, a net increase of about 3,000 people over ten years; an annual average of 7,900 openings includes replacement needs and is not the net increase per year or the number of job postings today.

OEWS wages exclude the self-employed, while EMP employment includes the self-employed; in the 2025 projection base for this occupation, the self-employed account for 24.4%. The two surveys cannot be combined directly to estimate the income of all workers.

Official annual wage estimates usually use a full-year, full-time basis of 2,080 hours, and this page cites the listed values directly. Individual actual hours, stoppages, costs, and taxes need separate verification, and an hourly quote multiplied by fixed hours is not treated as a personal income guarantee.

P10, P25, P50, P75, and P90 are employee wage positions, not skill levels or years of work experience. Personal comparison still requires verifying actual tasks, region, working hours, and pay composition.
